subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat plus cron expressions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining request defines new public scheduling semantics and config/protocol state that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a narrow every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit opt-in `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, persistence, docs, status display, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve current fixed anchored `every` semantics and treat the cron `every` part as not planned or requiring a separate proposal.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron, with migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit opt-in `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, persistence, docs, status display, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history on cron scheduler/stagger behavior and the product-boundary decision for extending schedule contracts.
